trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +90.03% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +51.59pp residual after beta, -32.2% max drawdown, 0.15% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +90.03% against the S&P 500's +14.41% over the same 251 sessions - an excess return of +75.62pp.
The momentum premium went against the declared exposure (-5.87% for a +1.0 loading) yet the account still returned +90.03% - the result was driven by something other than this factor.
The reversal premium this participant is built to harvest was live (-11.49% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
The beta premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+24.72% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
Of the +90.03% total, about +38.44pp is explained by carrying beta 2.67 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.33); the residual +51.59pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
RIVN contributed +52,138 USD (58% of net P&L) across 5 closed trades; TSLA was the biggest drag at -6,774 USD.
Execution cost 155 USD (0.15% of starting capital, 1.9 bp per fill, 1.8 bp of the 837,183 USD traded). 74% of that was spread/depth/impact and 26% was explicit fees and rebates.
14 closed round trips, 85.7% winners, profit factor 12.29, average winner +8,072 vs average loser -3,939 USD, median holding 74 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 251 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 1650 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: TSLA long 2025-09-17 to 2026-09-16, -6,774 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -32.18% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-03-27, recovered 2026-04-13. Average gross exposure 241% of starting capital, peak leverage 2.14x.
Daily returns were -0.10 skewed with excess kurtosis +1.67; historical 95% VaR -5.53%/day with CVaR -8.25%/day. Worst single session -14.03%, best +15.24%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.

Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: Momentum crashes when a beaten-down market rebounds sharply (high beta to the losing side); Monthly rebalancing means the signal is stale for up to 20 sessions; 2x gross leverage doubles the drawdown in a trend reversal.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 61.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @MomentumMax_12x1 (Momentum Max) ran the "cross-sectional momentum" archetype. Declared thesis: Rank the universe by trailing 63-session return with the most recent 5 sessions skipped, buy the top quartile and hold for a month. Winners keep winning because information diffuses slowly and investors under-react then herd. Entry: At the first session of each month, rank all 17 instruments by 63-session return, skipping the last 5 sessions; Buy the top 4 names in equal weight; Skip any name whose 63-session average dollar volume is below $100m (untradeable size). Exit: Rebalance to the new top 4 at the next month turn; No stop loss: the position is only exited at the rebalance. Sizing: equal weight, 50% of equity per name = 200% gross. Leverage: 2.0x gross (Reg T initial margin 50%). Cadence: monthly, horizon 1 month. Aggression 4/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Momentum has one of the largest documented premia in equities; levered and concentrated it is the highest-expected-return sleeve we can build from a single signal.
